lesson.grammar_point: be expected to / be supposed to / be meant to for norms and expectations

listenings.text: Hello Fabiana, this is Hafiz Rahman from Penang. Thank you for the call this morning. My director was very pleased that you greeted him first. Here, that is what a new partner is expected to do. I also want to explain something, so that nobody misreads it. When I was quiet during the forecast discussion, it did not mean that I agreed. In our team, we are not supposed to disagree with a figure in front of the director. I have some concerns about the October volumes, and I would like to touch base with you one to one. Our overlap is short, only one hour, from seven to eight in the morning your time. Could we speak on Thursday in that window? Until then, I will send my comments in writing, so we can work asynchronously. Thank you again for your patience with us after the fire.

Hi Fabiana, it's Lucia from the Monterrey plant. Welcome to the team. Before our first review, I wanted to share how we work here, so that nothing comes across as strange. First, our Monday call is meant to be a real conversation. We usually spend the first five minutes on how everyone is doing, and that is not wasted time. It is how we build trust. Second, people here are expected to answer the phone, even late in the day. Email is fine, but a quick call is often faster. Third, a small thing: please don't send requests on the sixteenth of September. It's our Independence Day, and a cost report that day would feel a little tone-deaf. Finally, we are supposed to send the daily handoff note to Penang by six p.m., but last week it was late twice. I'd like to fix that with you. With three sites, we can really follow the sun, but only if the handoff works.

extra_audio.text: Fabiana begins her guide by saying that the team works across three sites with three very different norms. First, she explains that in New York you are expected to raise problems in the meeting itself. Second, she writes that in Penang you are not supposed to put someone on the spot in front of their boss. Third, she says that in Monterrey the Monday call is meant to build trust before business. Then she explains that, because there is only one hour of overlap with Penang, most updates should be asynchronous. Finally, she reminds everyone that the handoff note is supposed to reach Penang by six p.m. Monterrey time, every day.

items.situation: A new analyst asks how to behave in the first call with Penang.
tips: You're expected to greet the director first, even if Hafiz does the talking.
be expected to + base verb: a norm other people count on.

items.situation: Your colleague wants to challenge Hafiz's numbers during the group call.
tips: We're not supposed to put someone on the spot in front of their boss. Let's touch base with him afterward.
not supposed to: not acceptable in that culture.

items.situation: New York asks why the Monterrey call starts with five minutes of personal conversation.
tips: The first five minutes are meant to build trust. It isn't wasted time.
be meant to: the purpose of something.

items.situation: The handoff note arrived in Penang three hours late. Tell Lucia, politely.
tips: The note was supposed to reach Penang by six, but it arrived at nine. Can we look at why?
was supposed to: expected in the past, but it didn't happen.

items.situation: Explain to your manager why most updates will be written, not live.
tips: We only have one hour of overlap with Penang, so most updates are meant to be asynchronous.
